The '''Expansionists''' were a [[faction]] that ruled in [[Sigil]] a thousand years ago. They believed that power was universal, and all things trended toward growth and improvement. The encouragement for people to be the best version of themselves they could be made them one of the most popular factions in Sigil.
== History ==
In [[874 BFHR]], in a meeting in the catacombs beneath [[Sigil]], twelve of the city's [[factol]]s met to beg the [[Lady of Pain]] to deal with the [[Expansionists]].<ref name="itc73">{{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|page=73}}</ref><ref name="uncaged42">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|page=42}}</ref><ref name="uncaged89">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|page=89}}</ref>
Shortly after, during a planning session for expanding his influence, Expansionist factol [[Vartus Timlin]] went for a walk to clear his head and was never seen again, having been sent to the [[Maze]]s.
The faction dissolved, with many members gravitating to the [[Believers of the Source]] or the [[Fated]]. All written references to the faction were stricken from the Rare and Dangerous Volumes Vault of the [[Hall of Records]]. Only one member still exists.
Rumors persist that Timlin has somehow escaped his Maze and is plotting his return to Sigil, and his revenge.
== Philosophy ==
The Expansionists believed power could be found anywhere, of all kinds, if only one was willing to harness it. All things trended towards improvement, so it was everyone's duty to improve themselves as much as possible. Many people took this self-help-guru advice and used it to become better people, the best versions of themselves. Unfortunately it also attracted a lot of thugs and brawlers, drawn to Timlin's force of personality and the promise of strength.
Eventually, Timlin's next step was enlarging the faction's influence to cover the entire city, including deposing the [[Lady of Pain]]. The other factions took exception to this, and hearing their cries for help, the Lady of Pain evidently agreed.
== Role ==
== Membership == : ''See also:'' [[List of Expansionist members]]
As a long-dead faction, the Expansionists are no longer accepting new members. The previous criteria for joining is unknown.
Only one member of the faction still exists: the [[Grixitt]], a mysterious creature who destroys the city's portals in retribution for the Lady's "crimes" against Timlin.

A '''faction''' is one of 15 philosophical organizations headquartered in [[Sigil]]. Each faction believes something different, with the understanding that in the [[Outer Planes]], belief shapes reality. While in Sigil, each faction has taken ownership of a different aspect of the smooth operation of the city's function. The factions engage in a sort of cold war over the beliefs of Cagers, called the ''[[kriegstanz]]''.
A "faction" without a headquarters in Sigil is referred to as a [[Sect]].
[[Outsider (Prime)|Outsider]]s (or "Clueless"), those visiting from the [[Prime Material plane]], are sometimes considered a pseudo-faction (of course, not one with any political sway). Once they've been around and have shaken off their ignorance enough to join a faction, they're no longer considered Clueless.
In modern Sigil, factions seem to be divided into two general classes: ''Ascendant factions'' are those larger factions more involved with the operation of the city, while ''minor factions'' are those who either more insular or simply don't much care about the politics of it all.
The governing of the city, such as it is, is done at the [[Hall of Speakers]]. Each faction -- at least each Ascendant faction -- has representation within the Hall, typically that faction's [[factol]]. There the factions can discuss, argue, negotiate, and collectively come up with new laws for Sigil. The laws are then enforced by the [[Harmonium]], [[Fraternity of Order]], and (if applicable) the [[Mercykillers]].
{{Factions}}
== History ==
The current status quo started [[503 BFHR|503 years before the reign of Factol Hashkar]], with an event called the [[Great Upheaval]].
There were previously 49 factions<ref name="fm81">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=81}}</ref>, with them each claiming their own slice of the Cage. During this time, power in the city was largely in the hands of the [[guild]]s, with factions being merely philosophical organizations. Eventually the factions broke out into all-out war. The [[Lady of Pain]] appeared before each factol with [[dabus]] to deliver a message:
: ''By order of the Lady of Pain, there will be but 15 factions in Sigil. Organize thy colors by a fortnight hence — or die.''
Inside two weeks, 34 factions dissolved, and Sigillians joined the remaining 15. Some refused, or didn't make the change fast enough, resulting in a purge of over 17,000 residents. Most joined up with the most "non-faction" faction, the [[Free League]], hoping to wait there for the whole thing to blow over. This shift made the Indeps the largest faction of all time with a million members. Within 50 years, however, that number had dropped to 20,000.<ref name="fm81">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=81}}</ref><ref name="fm3">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=3}}</ref><ref name="fw64">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=64}}</ref><ref name="fw114">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=114}}</ref><ref name="fw127">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=127}}</ref>
With the factions consolidated into 15, they found their power likewise consolidated, and began edging out the guilds for control of various parts of the city. One initiative was banning any faction member from membership in a guild, a move which reduced the numbers and strength of the latter. Eventually the factions took over. A handful of the larger guilds still exist, but at a fraction of their former strength.
A few individual factions rose and fell: around [[174 BFHR|300 years ago]], the [[Revolutionary League]] assassinated the factol of the [[Mercykillers]] and blamed it on the [[Fated]], setting off a conflict that involved 12 factions and resulted in the destruction of three factions.<ref name="fm114">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=114}}</ref>. But overall, 15 factions stood.
For many years, the factions were relatively stable, with a slight shakeup following the [[Faction War]] in [[130 YFHR|the 130th Year of Factol Hashkar's Reign]].

== Organization ==
All factions are unique, but their hierarchies can be generalized as follows:
* '''[[Factol]]s''' are those in charge of each respective faction. * '''[[Factor]]s''' are high-ups, those in charge of faction strongholds or seconds-in-command. * '''[[Factotum]]s''' are the lowest-ranking members who are still committed to the faction full-time. * '''[[Namer]]s''' are members "in name only." They're the vast majority of faction members, but continue to live their own lives, and may not consider the faction's philosophies beyond being able to make a surface-level argument in a pub.<ref name="dm21311">{{b|Dragon|Dragon Magazine 213|page=11}}</ref><ref name="fm3-4">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=3-4}}</ref>

The '''Faction War''' was an event that occurred in [[130 YFHR]] where Duke [[Rowan Darkwood]], [[Factol]] of the [[Fated]], made a play to take over [[Sigil]] from the [[Lady of Pain]].
== The War ==
The war involved all 15 factions going to war with each other. They split up into roughly three fronts:
* The "enemies of peace": The [[Doomguard]], the [[Free League]], the more violent Mercykillers (the [[Sodkillers]]), the [[Revolutionary League]], the [[Xaositects]] * The "oppressors of Sigil": The [[Believers of the Source]], the [[Fraternity of Order]], the [[Harmonium]], the less-violent Mercykillers (the [[Sons of Mercy]]), the [[Sign of One]], the [[Society of Sensation]] * The neutral factions: The [[Athar]], the [[Bleak Cabal]], the [[Dustmen]], the [[Fated]], the [[Mercykiller]] purists, and the [[Transcendent Order]]
{{stub}}
The following Factols end up [[Maze]]d:
* Factol [[Terrance]] of the [[Athar]] * Factol [[Ambar]] of the [[Believers of the Source]] * Factol [[Sruce]] of the [[Bleak Cabal]] * Factol [[Pentar]] of the [[Doomguard]] * Factol [[Skall]] of the [[Dustmen]] * Factol [[Rowan Darkwood]] of the [[Fated]] * [[Bria Tomay]] and her [[wemic]] entourage [[Lethea]] and [[Lysander]] * Several [[Revolutionary League]] cell leaders * Factol [[Darius]] of the [[Sign of One]] * Factol [[Erin Darkflame Montgomery]] of the [[Society of Sensation]] * Factol [[Karan]] of the [[Xaositects]]
The following Factols meet other fates:
* Factol [[Lhar]] of the [[Bleak Cabal]] succumbed to the [[Grim Retreat]] before the War broke out and appointed [[Sruce]] as his successor. * Factol [[Hashkar]] of the [[Fraternity of Order]] is murdered by a criminal released from the [[Prison]]. * Factol [[Sarin]] of the [[Harmonium]] is murdered by an Anarchist assassin just before the war breaks out. * Factol [[Alisohn Nilesia]] is sold by her new husband, Darkwood, as a slave to the fiends of the lower planes. * Factol [[Rhys]] senses what's going to happen, and leaves for [[Elysium]] before trouble breaks out. She orders her faction to keep out of "whatever's going to happen."
Rather than calm things down, the disappearance of their factols escalates tensions.

=== Aftermath ===
Two days after all parties declare a truce, the [[Lady of Pain]] reopens all portals. The next day, she appears before the new leaders of each faction, with a [[dabus]] in tow, to make a pronouncement:
:''This city tolerates your faction no longer. Abandon it or die.''
Cagers argue the exact meaning -- is "it" the city, or the faction? Is the exile forever? Can you be a member of a faction with a headquarters outside the city? -- but ultimately the factions know their time is at an end.
'''Abandon Your Faction''': Some factions remain in Sigil, but disband, at least for now. * The [[Bleak Cabal]] * The [[Dustmen]] * The [[Free League]] * The [[Society of Sensation]] * The [[Transcendent Order]] * The [[Xaositects]]
'''Abandon The City''': Some factions move their main power-base outside the city. Individual members can remain, however. * The [[Athar]] * The [[Doomguard]] * The [[Fated]] * The [[Fraternity of Order]] * The [[Harmonium]], now led by [[Faith]], the widow of Factol Sarin. * The [[Revolutionary League]]
'''Abandon Your (Current) Faction, And The City''': The remaining handful of factions changed form: * On their way out, the [[Believers of the Source]] and [[Sign of One]] found enough in common, and merged to form the [[Mind's Eye]], led by [[Ombidias]]. * The [[Mercykillers]] split back into their two original factions: ** The [[Sodkillers]] (with no real leader) remained in Sigil, although they call themselves the [[Minder's Guild]] until such a time as factions are allowed to operated again. ** The [[Sons of Mercy]] (led by [[Arwyl Swan's Son]]) also aren't a faction (for now), but maintain the Prison. They try to patrol the streets, but have no legal jurisdiction.

Since that time, the 15 factions have quietly conducted their philosophical battle for the hearts and minds of all Cagers - and always stopped short of all-out war. But now tensions are flaring, tempers are rising, and the Cage is about to explode into conflict!''

==Synopsis== The culmination of several adventures leading up to that point, ''The Faction War'' brought an end to the factions' control of the city. Instigated by the power-hungry Duke Rowan Darkwood, factol of the Fated, in a bid to dethrone the Lady of Pain and rule Sigil himself, the war spread throughout the city before the Lady of Pain, with the aid of a group of adventurers (the players' characters), intervened.

A '''factor''' (or less commonly, "factol's man") is a high-up member of a faction, often taking their orders directly from the [[factol]]. They oversee operations, commend strongholds, and otherwise do the work of governing the daily operations of their [[faction]].
When there's a vacancy, a factor is typically selected to take over as the new [[factol]].

==Description== Similar to the [[Elemental Plane of Water]], Fated Depths was a bottomless ocean without a surface. Unlike the [[Elemental Plane of Water|plane of water]], Fated Depths was under crushing pressure, briny, and produced no light—the only light sources were those belonging to the inhabitants. The waters were fouled with the effluent of the [[River of Blood]] to such an extent that it was effectively unholy water, capable of injuring any [[celestial]] being that came in contact with it.<ref name="PGtF-152" />
This plane had many connections to the Elemental Plane of Water and the water-dominant layers of the [[Abyss]]. A ''portal'' also existed between Fated Depths and [[Fury's Heart]], home of [[Umberlee]], the Bitch Queen. The usual [[Astral Plane]] methods of travel were possible, and the vomiting mouth of the River of Blood provided access to nearly all the other fiendish planes.<ref name="PGtF-152" /><ref name="PGtF-141">{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|141}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== Fated Depths was the typical [[afterlife]] destination for [[kuo-toa]]n and [[sahuagin]] [[petitioner]]s—they appeared in death just as they did in life. With many connections to the Abyss, there were an unusually large number of [[half-fiend]], half-sahaugin swimming in this plane. Demonic hybrids of kuo-toa were not uncommon either. Other inhabitants included such [[demon]]s and [[yugoloth]]s as [[myrmyxicus]]es, [[skulvyn]], [[piscoloth]]s, and [[wastrilith]]s, plus more natural creatures such as [[dire shark]]s, [[giant squid]], [[octopus]]es, and [[kraken]].<ref name="PGtF-152" /> Occasionally [[styx dragon]]s would leave the Blood River and be seen on this plane.<ref name="DoF-11" />
==Realms== * [[Blibdoolpoolp]] had a realm on this plane that was a moon-sized spherical temple that drifted through the murk, populated mainly by kuo-toan petitioners tending fiendish crustaceans and shellfish.<ref name="PGtF-152" /> * [[Sekolah]], the shark god of the sahuagin,<ref name="FaP-221">{{Cite book/Faiths and Pantheons|221}}</ref> prowled this plane with no particular demesne—his presence was the center of his realm, always moving through the brackish depths.<ref name="PGtF-152" />

'''Faxions''' refer to a series of [[faction]]s detailed in {{b|Dragon|Dragon Magazine 216}}, the April [[1995]] issue, in the ''April Fool's Faxions'' article.
Written by ''[[Factol's Manifesto (book)|Factol's Manifesto]]'' contributor [[Tim Beach]], the factions detailed within were ostensibly factions which had died out over the years. "They've all been extinct for a long time -- and maybe it's better that way." It should be noted that other than the article title, nothing within the article itself explicitly indicates that the contents are intended as an April Fools joke.
Given the canonical existence of groups like the [[Coterie of Cakes]] and [[Rosebringers]], despite the article being intended as a humorous April Fool's article, these factions -- or versions of them -- may be representative of some of the numerous factions which died out during the [[Great Upheaval]] or in the centuries since.

{{TOC limit|3}} ==Description== [[File:Feywild.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Feywild often appeared as dark and mysterious to many observers...]] The Feywild was a place of unrestrained and awe-inspiring natural beauty. The plane is always bathed in twilight of the setting (or perhaps rising) sun, with lanterns and fireflies providing additional, haunting lights.<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> Visitors to the plane found that all sensations, both sensory and emotional, were heightened. Smells were stronger, colors were more vivid, and sounds were clearer, but at the same time shadows were darker and impulses were harder to control.<ref name="MotP4e-p35"/> Strong emotions even altered the landscape of the Feywild itself, wilting flowers trailed the despondent or furious and carefree animals traveled alongside chipper and cheerful individuals.<ref name="DoD-p3" />
As an "echo" of the Prime Material plane, its geography was similar although not entirely identical to that of [[Toril]],<ref name="FRCG-p68" /> but the natural landscape was markedly more dramatic and beautiful in the Feywild, with mountains standing straighter and sharper, rivers flowing clearer and faster, flowers bloom brighter and more fragrantly,<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50" /><ref name="MotP4e-p35"/> and weather manifesting in supernatural ways.<ref name="DoD-p5">{{Cite book/Domains of Delight|5}}</ref> While most Prime locations and landmarks had analogues in the Feywild, sites of civilization in the Prime could be so unimportant in the Feywild as to be easily missed, while natural landmarks might be significantly more majestic or extreme. Navigating the Feywild was further complicated by the fact that distances did not always make sense. While two landmarks might be the same distance apart as in the Prime when travelling in one direction, they might be inexplicably further or closer on the return trip.<ref name="DoD-p3" /><ref name="MotP4e-p35">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|35}}</ref>
[[File:Feywild serene.png|thumb|right|300px|...but held some of the most beauteous locales in all the multiverse.]] Further complicating any visit to the plane was that time did not flow the same in the Feywild as on the Prime. While any visitor would experience time flowing as normal, it was often the case that more time was passing in the Prime, sometimes on the order of weeks, months, or years longer than expected,<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50" /><ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> although it was also possible for little or no time to have passed instead.<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50" /><ref name="DoD-p3" /> More concerning, leaving the Feywild could have dire consequences. Lost time could suddenly "catch up" to a mortal, sending them into fits of exhaustion or hunger, or even killing them instantly if many years had passed.<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> At the same time, those with no fey ancestry might find their memories of time spent in the Feywild going hazy, if not vanishing altogether.<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50" />
[[Arcane magic]] ran more freely and powerfully in the Feywild than it did in the Prime, and it was for this reason that so many of its inhabitants and landmarks were suffused with magic.<ref name="MotP4e-p35"/> As an additional consequence of this all-encompassing magic, arcane [[spells]] tended to be amplified in power or duration when cast in the Feywild,<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> and other times would manifest in entirely unexpected ways.<ref name="DoD-p4">{{Cite book/Domains of Delight|4}}</ref>
===Phenomena=== Motes of energy that originated in the Feywild manifested as ''[[feywild spark]]s''. These were highly sought after by adventurers that dared to brave the plane's perilous wilderness.<ref name="N.FF" />
It was believed the barrier between the Feywild and Toril was especially weak on [[Ches 19]] of the [[Calendar of Harptos]]. This occasion was celebrated as the holiday [[Fey Day]] in the [[Faerûn]]ian city of [[Waterdeep]].<ref name="W.DH-p184">{{Cite book/Waterdeep: Dragon Heist|184}}</ref>
The most common means of traversing in or out of the Feywild was through a [[fey crossroad]], which often required special knowledge of how to pass between the planes.<ref name="FRCG-p53">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|53}}</ref><ref name="SCAG-p138">{{Cite book/Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|138}}</ref>
===Flora & Fauna=== The Feywild was home to unique varieties of plant life, including various fungi that held supernatural properties. Notable among these were [[eldercap]]s, [[Executioner's Hood]]s, and [[hummingbrella]]s.<ref name="WBtW-p120">{{Cite book/The Wild Beyond the Witchlight|120}}</ref>
==Cosmography== The Feywild has had a unique relationship with the Prime Material plane, and consequently was in an unusual [[cosmology|cosmological]] position. ===Great Wheel Model=== Using the first iteration of the [[Great Wheel cosmology|Great Wheel]] cosmological model, the Faerie existed as one of the [[Outer Planes]], one that was coexistent with that of the Prime. This unique quality allowed creatures and fey beings could sometimes pass back-and-forth between the two planes at matching geographical locations without needing to traverse the [[Astral Plane]].<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> Indeed the Plane of Faerie held no connections to most [[transitive planes]], including the Astral Plane, [[Ethereal Plane]], or the [[Plane of Shadow]].<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/>
[[File:4e FR cosmology.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] cosmological model asserted the Feywild was a parallel "echo" of the mortal Realms, akin to the contrasting [[Shadowfell]].]] During this era, each location on the Prime held a duplicate in Faerie, albeit one altered in form and appearance by the plane's unique traits.<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> Additionally, Faerie maintained some traits that were not observable during other times of history, such as lighter force of gravity than that felt on the Prime.<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/>
Faerie's other planar traits, like the aforementioned [[Feywild#Passage of Time|extended perception of the passage of time]], were experienced by planar travelers following the reintroduction of the Great Wheel model that coincided with the [[Second Sundering]] of Toril and [[Abeir]]. New phenomena became apparent as well, such as incidents of memory loss expressed by these individuals. This second iteration of the Great Wheel model of the plane came to be known as the Feywild, following its [[Feywild#World Axis|World Axis]] predecessor, and retained the distinction of existing as a [[parallel plane]].<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50" /><ref name="MTF-p49" />
===World Tree Model=== The plane of Faerie was notably absent from the [[World Tree cosmology|World Tree]] cosmological model that came into wide use for about just over a decade during the late 14{{th}} century [[DR]].<ref name="PGtF-p140">{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|140}}</ref><ref name="FRCS3e-p256-258">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|256-257}}</ref> This omission may have been linked to the continual weakening of the bond between Faerie and Toril,<ref name="SK-p55" /> and the then-recent mass migration of [[elves]] back to Evermeet, referred to as [[the Retreat]].<ref name="FRCS3e-p123">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|123}}</ref>
===World Axis=== The late 14{{th}} century world even known as the [[Spellplague]], led to a re-adjustment of the planes and the adoption of the [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] cosmological model.<ref name="FRCG-p50">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|50}}</ref> The Feywild as it was then called, was recreated as one of the parallel planes,<ref name="MotP4e-p34"/> an "echo" of the Prime<ref name="DMG4e-p161">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 4th edition|161}}</ref> that remained as such even following the Second Sundering.<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50" />
Travel between the Feywild and the Prime became relatively easy for many inhabitants of each plane, as the boundary between them was quite thin, and in some cases there were regions which existed in an overlapping space between the two,<ref name="FRCG-p68" /> a phenomenon sometimes called [[worldfall]].<ref name="MotP4e-p34"/> Unlike its pre-Spellplague iteration, the Feywild was linked by passageways to the [[Astral Sea]].<ref name="FRCG-p62">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|62}}</ref> Well-protected and often dangerous connections linked the Feywild with the [[astral dominion]]s of [[Arvandor]], the [[Deep Wilds]], and the [[Gates of the Moon]].<ref name="FRCG-p68">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|68}}</ref>
==Notable Locations== Though much of the Feywild was the same as the Prime geographically, there were differences, and more importantly, the lands answered to different powers than those on Toril. Much of the [[elf|elven]] or [[fey eladrin|eladrin]] civilizations had their earliest roots here and abandoned remnants of their culture littered the landscape. Unlike the elves, however, who had all but abandoned the Feywild, some eladrin remained behind in the Feywild, most notably the "[[Noble eladrin|noble]]" eladrin, who maintained strong kingdoms and citadels.<ref name="FRCG-p68" /><ref name="SCAG-p138"/> Some notable elven cities and settlements were located at points where the barrier between the planes was extremely thin, and as a result they existed in both the Prime and the Feywild simultaneously. Such locations included [[Evermeet]],<ref name="SCAG-p72">{{Cite book/Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|72}}</ref> [[Evereska]],<ref name="FRCG-p130">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|130}}</ref> and [[New Sharandar]].<ref name="NCS-p177">{{Cite book/Neverwinter Campaign Setting|177}}</ref>
Some regions in the Feywild were known to attune to the most powerful creature nearby, fey or otherwise. These regions would warp to reflect the emotion or attitude of the creature to which they were attuned, with everything from the weather to the landscape changing to be more dismal, peaceful, or dangerous as best befitted the creature's mood. However, a creature could not exert direct or conscious control over their demesne.<ref name="MotP4e-p35"/>
===Realms=== [[File:Feywild map.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A map of the Feywild, showing the relative locations of various cities and realms.]] ; [[Brokenstone Vale]] : The Feywild kingdom of [[lycanthrope]]s attracted outcasts and refugees from across the realms of mortals. It had a long and bloodied history, have been founded by a [[werewolf]] lord that fought for his people's freedom from the neighboring eladrin. Despite its past, Brokenstone's residents garnered benefits from choosing to remain in the Feywild that were unavailable to their kin that dwelled on the Prime.<ref name="MotP4e-p42">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|42}}</ref><ref name="HotF-p14">{{Cite book/Player's Option: Heroes of the Feywild|14}}</ref> ; [[Iliyanbruen]] : The elven survivor-state of the ancient Faerûnian realm of [[Illefarn]] was reformed in the Feywild following its near-complete destruction on Toril. The Iliyanbruen elves were perceived as invaders by the native fey, and were forced to fight for their new home for many centuries.<ref name="NCS-p12-13">{{Cite book/Neverwinter Campaign Setting|12-13}}</ref><ref name="NCS-p28">{{Cite book/Neverwinter Campaign Setting|28}}</ref> ; [[Nachtur]] : One of the most powerful [[goblin]] kingdoms in all the Feywild. It was labyrinth of underground warrens ruled over by the [[Gark|Great Gark]], Lord of All the Goblins. Gark commanded a host of mercenaries that served many malevolent beings such as [[hag]]s and Winter Fey lords.<ref name="MotP4e-p46">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|46}}</ref><ref name="DunMag196-p4">{{Cite dungeon/196/Backdrop: The Moonshae Isles|4}}</ref><ref name="HotF-p18">{{Cite book/Player's Option: Heroes of the Feywild|18}}</ref> ; [[Realm of Malabog]] : The domain of [[Malabog]], the fomorian king that extended his area of conquest beyond the Feydark into the wilderness up above.<ref name="N.FF">{{Cite game/Neverwinter: Fury of the Feywild}}</ref>
Additionally, the demiplane of [[Sildëyuir]], the home of the [[star elf|star elves]], was at times said to be part of the Feywild, where it was said to occupy the location there that corresponded to the [[Yuirwood]] of the Material plane.<ref name="FRCG-p68" />
===Settlements=== [[File:Cendriane_Ruins.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A [[gnome]] adventurer plays hide-and-seek with a [[displacer beast]].]] * [[Astrazalian]], the eladrin City of Starlight governed by Lady Shandria, niece of Titania.<ref name="MotP4e-p41">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|41}}</ref> * [[Cendriane]], an ancient city that was taken over by the [[eladrin]] [[vampire lord|vampire]] named [[Kannoth|Lord Kannoth]].<ref name="HotF-p14" /><ref name="MotP4e-p42">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|42}}</ref><ref name="Dr391-p67">{{Cite dragon/391/Watchers at the Living Gate|67}}</ref> * [[Evermeet]], the center of Elven culture on Faerûn was transported to the Feywild for over a Torillian century, following the Spellplague.<ref name="FRCG-p132">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|132}}</ref> * [[Mithrendain]], the Autumn City of the Feywild was built atop a perilous passageway leading down to the Feydark below.<ref name="MotP4e-p45">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|45}}</ref> * [[Shinaelestra]], the Fading City of [[ranger]]s that wavered between the Feywild and the [https://tahlequahpointsoflight.fandom.com/wiki/Howling_Forest?action=edit&redlink=1 Howling Forest] on the world of [[Nerath]].<ref name="MotP4e-p46-47">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|46-47}}</ref><ref name="HotF-p149">{{Cite book/Player's Option: Heroes of the Feywild|149}}</ref>
===Feydark=== The [[Feydark]] was the echo of Toril's [[Underdark]] in the Feywild. Like most parts of the Feywild, it was more majestic and fantastic than its natural counterpart, with cavernous maze-like tunnels filled with exotic [[fungi]].<ref name="MotP4e-p43">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|43}}</ref> [[File:Malabog'sCastle.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Not all fomorians remained within the Underdark. King [[Malabog]] ruled his vast kingdom from his [[Malabog's Castle|mighty castle]].]] ; [[Mag Tureah]] : The most powerful of the Feydark's [[fomorian]] realms stood within a country-sized cavern lit by precious gems and stones. This kingdom was ruled by the fomorian king [[Bres]].<ref name="FRCG-p68" /><ref name="HotF-p16" /> ; [[Vor Thomil]] : This filthy subterranean realm was ruled by the malevolent fomorian Queen [[Connomae]]. Outsiders captured by the resident giants were mocked and humiliated for the queen's amusement, forced to masquerade as courtiers her a twisted mockery of royal assembly.<ref name="MotP4e-p46-47" /><ref name="HotF-p16">{{Cite book/Player's Option: Heroes of the Feywild|16}}</ref>
===Domains of Delight=== {{Main|Domains of Delight}} Within the Feywild were numerous [[demiplanes]] created by the [[Archfey]], independent realms that were each formed to reflect the whims and and emotions of its creator.<ref name="DoD-p3">{{Cite book/Domains of Delight|3}}</ref> They grew or shrunk in size depending on the power of their Archfey, occasionally leading to discontent among their leaders when borders of neighboring domains overlapped with one another.<ref name="DoD-p5">{{Cite book/Domains of Delight|5}}</ref>
One of the more prominent domains of delight was [[Prismeer]], the realm of [[Zybilna]].<ref name="WBtW-p15">{{Cite book/The Wild Beyond the Witchlight|15}}</ref> The domain was shattered by the [[Hourglass Coven]] of [[hag]]s and reformed as three splinter-realms of [[Hither]], [[Thither]], and [[Yon]].<ref name="WBtW-p57">{{Cite book/The Wild Beyond the Witchlight|57}}</ref>
Also found within Prismeer was the lesser domain of [[Fablerise]]. This gloomy forest was created by [[Yarnspinner]], an enormous fey spider that attracted myriad ''[[awaken]]ed'' animals with his near endless supplies of stories and tales.<ref name="DoD-p22">{{Cite book/Domains of Delight|22}}</ref>
==History== ===Formation and Connection to Toril=== {{Quote|But tales are told of a time long past, when elves fled by the thousands from war-torn Faerie, that magical land that exists in the unseen shadows of a thousand worlds.|Excerpt from a letter from [[Kriios Halambar]], Master Luthier of [[New Olamn]].<ref name="E.IE">{{Cite book/Evermeet: Island of Elves}}</ref>}}
The Feywild was created by the [[Primordial]]s, beings of power comparable with the [[deity|gods]]. Finding some things of the Prime too "bright" or too "dark," the primordials tore these parts from the Prime, creating the Feywild and the Plane of Shadow (later known as the Shadowfell), respectively.<ref name="DMG4e-p161" /> It was believed that the original [[Deity|deities]] worshiped by the elves, the [[Faerie gods]] of the [[Seelie Court]],<ref name="TGHotR-p8"/> originated in the Feywild.<ref name="FRCG-p68" /> The first creatures to join them in this world were the fey, and came in many forms. ''Circa'' [[-34000 DR]],<ref name="SK-p186">{{Cite book/Serpent Kingdoms|186}}</ref> the plane came to be ruled by a mysterious [[fey creator race]], who gave rise to the first [[korred]]s, [[Sprite (creature)|sprites]], and [[pixie]]s.<ref name="TGHotR-p7">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|7}}</ref>
The first record of the fey immigrating to [[Abeir-Toril]] from Faerie—as the plane was previously called—came about ''circa'' [[-27000 DR]]. This great migration included [[lythari]], [[avariel]], and [[green elves]],<ref name="RoF-p27">{{Cite book/Races of Faerûn|27}}</ref> ancestors of the [[wild elves]] and [[dark elves]],<ref name="TGHotR-p8"/> and [[eladrin]],<ref group="note">The ''[[Forgotten Realms Player's Guide]]'' uses the term "green elves" to refer to these eladrin.</ref> ancestors of the other elven races.<ref name="FRPG-p15">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Player's Guide|15}}</ref> The Fey ushered the elves to Toril, hoping the then-primitive creatures would help bring down the reign of [[dragon]]s.<ref name="TGHotR-p8"/> It was at this time that the ancient elves began their split into the [[Tel'Quessir]] of Toril and the [[fey eladrin|eladrin]] of the Feywild.<ref name="MTF5e-p49-50"/>
Some centuries later, ''circa'' [[-25400 DR]], a small group of [[gold elves]] and [[silver elves]] also arrived on Toril following a magical experiment gone terribly awry that destroyed the island of [[Tintageer]] in Faerie.<ref name="TGHotR-p8"/><ref name="EIotE-p93-96">{{Cite book/Evermeet: Island of Elves/MMP|93-96}}</ref>
During their millennium on Toril, the [[Noble eladrin|eladrin]] established numerous realms that were more-closely linked to Faerie that other locations across the world.<ref name="FRCG-p68" />
===Separation=== In the {{Yearlink|-2549}}, local [[drow]] introduced the [[Susurrus]] to the [[Shadowdale|Living Wood]] in the [[Eastern Heartlands]], severing the bond between the resident fey and the plane of Faerie.<ref name="S.SotL-p114">{{Cite book/Shadowdale: The Scouring of the Land|114}}</ref>
Around the {{YearlinkName|-500}}, most of the fey of the [[Moonshae Isles]], including the [[LeShay]] and [[fomorian]] giants, left their home on Toril for Faerie. The isle of [[Karador]] sank beneath the waters of the waters of the [[Sea of Swords]].<ref name="DragMag362" />
After the fall of [[Iliyanbruen]] in the 2{{nd}} century [[DR]],<ref name="TGHotR-p66">{{Cite book/The Grand History of the Realms|66}}</ref> some elves retreated for the isle of [[Evermeet]], yet others opted for another solution. A group of these elves actually transported Iliyanbruen's capital [[Sharandar]] back to the Plane of Faerie.<ref name="NCS-p28">{{Cite book/Neverwinter Campaign Setting|28}}</ref>
Over the millennia, the Plane of Faerie had slipped further and further away from the Prime, although they still remained inextricably linked.<ref name="MotP3e-p210"/> By the late 14{{th}} century DR, the weakening of the bond between Faerie and Toril was observed by scholars from the continent of [[Faerûn]].<ref name="SK-p55">{{Cite book/Serpent Kingdoms|55}}</ref>
===Reconnection=== [[File:NewSharandar - Howard Lyon.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The fey settlement of [[New Sharander]] was the beneficiary of the renewed connection between the Feywild and the Prime. The city coexisted between both planes, linked by the ''[[Fey Crossing]]'' portal.]] This relationship between the two planes was reversed entirely when the [[Spellplague]] struck in the {{YearlinkName|1385}}, although the exact reasons for this remain unclear.<ref name="FRCG-p68" /> It could have been related to increased traffic between the Feywild and the Moonshae Isles during the preceding decade,<ref name="FRCG-p152">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|152}}</ref><ref name="DragMag362">{{Cite dragon/362/Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes}}</ref>{{Speculation}} or the significant number of realms that had been built by the eladrin over the course of centuries.<ref name="FRCG-p68" />
Regardless of the cause, the Feywild was yanked back into proximity with the Prime, and new [[fey crossroad|crossroads]]<ref name="FRCG-p68" /> and [[faerie pool]]s were opened up across the Realms.<ref name="FRCG-p215">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|215}}</ref> [[Evermeet]] slipped into the Feywild,<ref name="FRCG-p132">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|132}}</ref> as did the demiplane of [[Sildëyuir]].<ref name="FRCG-p68" /> At the same time, the eladrin of the Feywild found themselves newly reconnected to the elven peoples of Toril.<ref name="FRCG-p5">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|5}}</ref>
Since the barrier between these two planes became much thinner, the eladrin discovered that they could slip easily between the Feywild and the Prime at sites of great elven magic and importance, such as Evermeet,<ref name="FRCG-p132" /> [[Evereska]],<ref name="FRCG-p130"/> and [[Sarifal]].<ref name="FRCG-p152">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|152}}</ref> Ironically, the recently-raised elven city of [[Myth Drannor]] was almost completely closed off from the Feywild.<ref name="FRCG-p156-157">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|156-157}}</ref>
Some time during or after the {{YearlinkName|1479}}, the fomorian king [[Malabog]] forged an alliance with the [[Toril]]lian [[lich]] [[Valindra Shadowmantle]] and prepared to invade the Realms by means of the transitive city of [[New Sharandar]]. The giant-king's war ended before it began, due to the intervention of [[Heroes of Sleeping Dragon Bridge|adventurers]] from [[Neverwinter]].<ref name="N.FF">{{Cite game/Neverwinter: Fury of the Feywild}}</ref>
With the end of the [[Second Sundering]], the Feywild remained closely tied to the Prime<ref name="DMG5e-p49-50"/> and Evermeet returned to Toril, although it dwelt in a state of coexistence between the Prime, the Feywild, and [[Arvandor]].<ref name="SCAG-p72"/><ref name="MTF-p49">{{Cite book/Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes|49}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== [[File:ElfInTheFeywild.jpg|thumb|right|250px|''An [[elf]] in the Feywild.'']] The inhabitants of the Feywild varied in temperament from kind to malicious, but almost all had a mischievous side to them and few stopped to consider the needs or worries of visitors to their home. While many of those living in Faerie were untamed, large numbers also congregated according to race or by political allegiance.<ref name="FRCG-p68" /><ref name="MotP3e-p211">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|211}}</ref> Just as the geography was reminiscent of [[Toril]]'s, some of its inhabitants existed as fey "echoes" of Prime creatures.<ref name="FRCG-p68" />
All manner of [[fey]] species were found within the Feywild.
The [[leShay]] were an enigmatic species that were among the Feywild's most powerful inhabitants;<ref>{{Cite book/Epic Level Handbook|202-203}}</ref> though the various [[archfey]] were undoubtedly even more powerful.<ref>{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|36}}</ref>
[[Fey eladrin]] were the beings that had the closest thing to a civilization in the Feywild.<ref name="MotP4e-p39">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|39}}</ref> They were the descendants of the elves that never left the Feywild, and over the millennia had become suffused with the plane's primal magic.<ref name="MTF5e-p195">{{Cite book/Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes|195}}</ref>
Other creatures that dwelled within the Feywild included [[moonstone dragon|moonstone]],<ref>{{Cite book/Fizban's Treasury of Dragons|211}}</ref> [[mirage dragon|mirage]],<ref>{{Cite book/Draconomicon: Chromatic Dragons|196}}</ref> and [[faerie dragon|faerie]] dragons; [[fomorian]]s and their servitor [[cyclops|cyclopes]] ruled much of the Feydark;<ref>{{Cite book/Monster Manual 4th edition|110}}</ref> and [[harengon]], who were blessed with good fortune.<ref>{{Cite book/The Wild Beyond the Witchlight|13}}</ref> [[Goblinoid]]s, [[ogre]]s, [[giant]]s, and [[blight]]s could all be found in the more sinister regions of the plane.<ref>{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|43,51-52}}</ref>
===Seelie and Unseelie Fey=== Most but not all fey served one of two [[Deity|godlike]] [[archfey]] queens, [[Titania|Titania the Summer Queen]] or the [[Queen of Air and Darkness]], who shared an ancient and bitter rivalry.<ref name="DMG5e-p49" /> Those who belonged to Titiana's [[Seelie Court (divine realm)|Seelie Court]] were known as [[seelie fey]], and were generally [[good]]-aligned and represented or celebrated the beauty of nature. They were known to be honorable toward visitors to the Feywild, if a bit mischievous, but they did not welcome non-fey to join their Court. Those who belonged to the Queen of Air and Darkness's [[Unseelie Court]] were known as unseelie fey, and were generally [[evil]]-aligned and represented or celebrated the darker and more macabre aspects of the natural world. They were generally more dangerous and untrustworthy in their dealings with visitors, however they were known to be more welcoming of non-fey into their Court.<ref name="SCAG-p138"/><ref name="MotP4e-p38">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 4th edition|38}}</ref><ref name="FF">{{Cite web/Fey Feature/Seelie and Unseelie Courts}}</ref> The Unseelie Court worked tirelessly to undermine the Seelie Court, sometimes violently but more often through games and cruel mischief.<ref name="DMG5e-p49" /><ref name="FF"/>
The remaining inhabitants of the Feywild either held no allegiances except at their own whims, or served another of the archfey, such as [[Oberon]], [[Hyrsam]], or the [[Prince of Frost]].<ref name="SCAG-p138"/> Uglier inhabitants of the Feywild, such as fomorians and hags, were generally not welcome among either the Seelie or Unseelie Courts.<ref name="DMG5e-p49" />
===Notable Inhabitants=== * [[Dara Algwynenn Kalinoth]], a moon elf princess that became the prophet of the [[Cult of the Howling Hatred]].<ref name="PotA-p12" /><ref name="PotA-p193">{{Cite book/Princes of the Apocalypse|193}}</ref> * [[Sharlario Moonflower]], one of the first elves to emigrate from Faerie to Toril.<ref name="E.IE-p98-107">{{Cite book/Evermeet: Island of Elves/MMP|98-107}}</ref>

''Forgotten Realms'' is a [[Dungeons & Dragons]] Campaign Setting, and was generally considered the default D&D setting during the AD&D 2nd Edition era, and again during D&D 5th Edition. It's a high-magic medieval fantasy world, with ancient cultures capable of incredible magical feats, and gods who often incarnate as Avatars to meddle in the affairs of the world.
The ''Forgotten Realms'' takes place in the world of [[Toril]], in the [[Prime Material plane]]. As a high-magic setting, the residents of Toril have familiarity with planars and portals, and can often be found in the planes.
{{quote|No, that's it. Toril has all those realms, and... I can't seem to remember anything about them.|[[Romas Tried]], planar sage}}

Planescape races "escape containment": [[Tiefling]]s and [[eladrin]] are introduced to FR as PC races in the ''Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting''.
=== 5th Edition ===
In 1358 DR (approximately [[119 YFHR]]), a warlock coven enacted a ritual on Toril, cursing all tieflings in the world to have the "mark of Asmodeus" -- effectively rewriting all tieflings such that their ancestry could be traced to [[Asmodeus]]. This was a gambit to make him the "racial god" over the world's tieflings, allowing him to ascend to full godhood on [[Toril]].
The plan came to fruition in 1385 DR after the Spellplague, making Asmodeus a god.
Accordingly, for decades afterward, Toril's tieflings all had a similar appearance, owing to their shared ancestry: primarily reddish skin, a tail, and horns. Obviously, the sudden transformation of the world's tieflings to have a pronounced demonic appearance caused an increase in mistrust towards and already distrusted race.<ref name="scag118">{{b|D&D|Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|page=118}}</ref>
Tieflings of other ancestry (and appearance) continued to exist in other worlds and planes.<ref name="tcoe118">[[Rhys]] appears on {{b|D&D|Tasha's Cauldron of Everything|page=103}}</ref>

{{Quote|''Welcome to the best-loved and best-known town of the Outlands - we know you'll agree.''|Anton Levelskill of the Harmonioum<ref name="APPttO-p17" />}}
==Description== Fortitude had neat roads and wide boulevards and was filled with fountains, luscious parks, groves and orchards. Only about half the town included actual buildings. Most of the buildings were several stories high, with the lower level made from stone and the upper levels of wood and mud topped by thatched roofs. The gate-town was home to several inns.<ref name="APPttO-p17" />
The gate-town was surrounded by a large wall in the shape of a perfect oval, hence the gate-town's nickname "The Egg". At one end of the town was the gate to Arcadia, and the other end was a stadium called the Confessional. The wall was dotted with several small entrances into the town.<ref name="APPttO-p17" />
===Gates=== Sitting atop a circular pyramid made from seven tiers, the Gate to Arcadia appeared as a large green flame. One merely had to step into the flame to travel to the plane.<ref name="APPttO-p17"/>
===The Confessional=== This arena was constructed within a great pit in the ground. The craftsmanship of the stonework was superb, allowing for even the quietest of sounds to echo loudly throughout the arena. The primary purpose of the arena was as a location for individuals to announce the repentance of sins and accept punishment. A crowd gathered several times a week to hear the admittance of faults from confessors. It was a popular event since it was the crowd itself that determined punishment. Punishment varied and depended on the mood of the crowd. If a confessor refused punishment, they were jailed for their own protection. Despite this, many individuals volunteered freely to confess their misdeeds and sins.<ref name="APPttO-p17"/>
==Government== Fortitude was ruled by a council of seven called the Secret Conclave. The entire Conclave was replaced by new members each time the [[Great Modron March]] visited the gate-town. During this even, the residents elected seven new members who were citizens of Fortitude. The winners of the election were kept secret.<ref name="APPttO-p17" />

It was a place of boiling, molten earth and toxic fumes. ==Geography== The plane was a vast mountain range of volcanoes that started at the border with the Plane of Earth and extended well into the Plane of Fire, forming an arc around the vast [[Cinder Wastes]]. There were also many floating islands of volcanic rock that had not yet fully liquified. Much of the air on this plane was [[acid]]ic and [[poison]]ous. Its clouds were composed of burning acidic vapors and raw [[elemental fire]]. Temperatures were close to that of the Plane of Fire. Most unprotected fluids and water brought into the plane boiled away near instantly into superheated vapor.{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|76}} ===Cosmography=== Lava flowing from the Fountains of Creation into the Plane of Earth formed a region known as the [[Furnaces]], where the [[dao]] inhabitants of the plane used the lava to power their forges.{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|54}} The Fountains of Creation were considered to have some of the most abundant [[elemental vortex|elemental vortices]] of all the para-elemental planes, occurring in the heart of almost every active volcano on the [[Prime Material plane]]. ===Flora & Fauna=== Some of the more bestial elementals to be found on this plane included [[fire bat]]s, [[thoqqua]], a large number of [[animental]]s, and small animate burning rocks known as [[blazon (creature)|blazons]]. One of the few flora that could be found on this plane was the magical [[tandersol]], a plant whose stem was pure fire and leaves were metallic [[gold]]. People often braved the hazards of this plane to obtain those leaves, as they could be used to make ''+3 [[scale armor]]'' that had resistance to heat and flame. ==Notable Locations== * [[Oolan's laboratory]], the small workshop of an [[Oerth]]ian [[lich]] named [[Oolan]] that was situated in the Scorched Wastes. * [[Targath's tower]], a tower constructed out of invisible, permanent [[wall of force|''walls of force'']] by [[wizard]]s commissioned by a [[thief]] named [[Targath Reniume]].{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|79}} * [[Thermax]], a vast [[fire giant]] fortress-city situated at the nexus of a number of lava tubes.{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|78}} ===Boundary Regions=== * '''Obsidian Forest''', the reaches of this plane closest to the [[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Minerals|Plane of Minerals]]. Here lava cooled into a smooth plain of hard [[obsidian]], with spires of geode-like crystal and volcanic glass. Creatures of elemental stone infested this area, having fled from their ruler [[Ogrémoch]].{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|74}} * '''Scorched Wastes''', the reaches of this plane closest to the Plane of Earth. It was a largely uninhabited area of [[basalt]] cliffs and spires with lakes and rivers of lava. ==Inhabitants== The Fountains of Creation were the birthplace of most of the [[lava child]]ren and [[magmin]]. The latter lived in small, hunter-gather tribes{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/Monstrous Supplement|12-13}} that were united, while the former dwelt in small underground communities and were frequently trying to avoid enslavement by the dao that came to the plane. The magmin often struck bargains with elementals and para-elementals, but had no love for [[mephit]]s. This plane was also the native realm of [[magma para-elemental]]s, who along with [[magma mephit]]s were the most commonly encountered creature on this place. Magma para-elementals had no set leaders among them,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II 1st edition|98-99}} no borders, and lacked internal conflicts. They also had good relations with the plane's magmin. The magma mephits that inhabited this plane were always feuding with [[fire mephit]]s, while magma para-elementals waged war on both types.{{Cite book/Monstrous Compendium Planescape Appendix III|10}} Though they generally tried to avoid conflict with magma mephits when they could, as they were undoubtedly the reigning race on that plane. Fire giants primarily lived within Thermax, but could be found in strongholds scattered throughout the plane. They and many other natives made their homes on floating islands of volcanic rock. Fire giants could also be found living inside the volcanoes of this plane, as could [[azer]]s, [[red dragon]]s, and native inhabitants of both the Plane of Earth and the Plane of Fire. Many inhabitants of the plane were known to engage in warfare with the dao,{{Cite book/Monstrous Compendium Planescape Appendix III|6}} who sailed across the surface of the plane's magma on [[obsidian]] ships. The ones that did the most to keep them in check was a large force of [[efreet]], though it was not always conflict between them, as sometimes dao and efreet met on this plane to do trade. When it came to enslavement, the dao primarily targeted magmin and mephits.{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|28}} ==Rumors & Legends== Some rumors claimed that a race of black skinned [[humanoid]]s that spoke sideways lived amid the steam that rose from this plane's magma. In addition, some regions of this plane's magma sea were rumored to contain schools of deadly [[fish]] that had been magically altered to thrive in the lava.{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|77}} ==Appendix== {{Incomplete}} ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Para-Elemental Planes]] [[Category:Inner Planes]] [[Category:Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]]

The '''Fraternity of Order''' are a [[faction]] believe that the multiverse can be defined by a series of rules. And once you know and understand these rules, you can exploit them.
== History ==
* [[856 BFHR]]: The Fraternity of Order becomes an organized group, establishing the rules for chartering a [[faction]]. Accordingly, since they were the first chartered under their own rules, the Guvners consider themselves the first and oldest faction. (Other factions may disagree.)<ref name="fm69">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=69}}</ref> * [[574 BFHR]]: The time of Fraternity of Order [[Factol]] [[Jaretta]]. "Anarchists" are mentioned in Guvner records during this time, who may or may not be the same group as the eventual [[Revolutionary League]].<ref name="fm114">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=114}}</ref> * [[1 YFHR]]: Fraternity of Order [[Factol]] [[Lariset]] the Inescapable spends several months sequestered in research before vanishing from her quarters. == Philosophy ==
Everything has laws; most are dark. Learn the laws of the multiverse and you can rule it.
The Guvners divide laws into three rough categories: ''Rules'' define what individual people do, ''Laws'' define societies and the natural world, and ''Great Axioms'' are laws governing the multiverse and empowering the gods. Guvners seek to discover all the Great Axioms, but even the highest-ranking Guvners usually only know a bare handful.
=== Branches ===
The [[Mathematicians]] are a sect which splintered off from the Guvners, being more attracted to the mysteries of the gears of Mechanus than even the main faction.
== Role ==
The Fraternity of Order affinity for rules and laws makes them perfect for running the High Courts, the seat of Sigil's legal system. They write the laws and adjudicate over criminal trials in the courtrooms (as both judges and lawyers). The Harmonium enforce the laws, and once a criminal is deemed guilty, they're passed on to the Mercykillers to carry out the punishment.
== Membership ==
: ''See also:'' [[List of Fraternity of Order members]]
The Guvners require at least a few hours of service each week from every member of the faction. Accordingly, faction ranks are usually based on the court system.
; '''[[Namer]]s'''
Namers are typically titled '''Aides''', particularly during their work in the courts. Aides must follow the orders of any Administrator, unless that order conflicts with another ongoing task.
; '''[[Factotum]]s'''
Factotums are titled '''Administrators'''. In order to become an Administrator, every 100 days a series of tests is issued, which an Aide must pass. One of these tests is being able to demonstrate a special ability based on their understanding of a loophole in the multiverse. Loophole powers may take months to discover.
Successfully passing gives the new Administrator an A10 ranking. Ranks then proceed up to A1, with a new test available every 100 days (a particularly good score may result in advancing two ranks). Lower-ranked Administrators may feel like glorified Aides. Higher ranked Administrators may have Aides of their own to supervise.
Administrators of all ranks serve as legal advisers as well as attorneys.
''Benefits'': Administrators of at least 5th level gain a limited ability to manipulate probability: 1/day they may gain a +1 to an attack roll, damage roll, or saving throw, or a -1 bonus to roll against a proficiency or ability score, or adjust a percentage roll by 5%. Additionally, they may give a -1/5% penalty to an opponent's roll. These bonuses and penalties gain an additional ±1/5% every three levels.
; '''[[Factor]]s'''
Factors are known as '''Bureau Chiefs''', and serve as judges. Similar to the test to become Administrators, A1-ranked factotums may take at test in order to become a Bureau Chief. However, there are a set number of Chiefs, and advancement can only happen if an existing position is vacant.
Bureau Chiefs are rated from B5 to B1. Lower-ranked Chiefs supervise lesser bureaus, which are often part of larger bureaus. B1s supervise the Star Bureaus, which have been around for centuries: Record-Keeping, Research, Internal Affairs, Planar Affairs, and Prime Affairs. B2s may supervise Ad Hoc bureaus, which are technically considered temporary, despite some of them having been around for a century or more, such as the Bureau of Courts, which assigns court duty to faction members.

The '''Free League''' are a [[faction]], although if you ask most Indeps, they'll deny it. The idea that anyone knows the truth and everyone else is wrong? Since when does a smart gambler risk it all on a single throw?
== History ==
The Indeps have been around for centuries. During the [[Great Upheaval]] in [[503 BFHR]], the Lady's pronouncement to whittle down the numbers of factions down to 15 had most of Sigil's population switching allegiance to the Free League, the most non-faction faction, figuring they'd just wait for the whole thing to blow over and figure out which of the surviving factions to join. The Free League had the honor of becoming the largest faction in Sigil's history, with a million members.
By [[453 BFHR]], within fifty years of the Upheaval, that number was down to 20,000. Some of that was due to people joining other factions once the new 15 had been established, but a large part of it was a "plague" which swept through the faction.
After the [[Faction War]], when the Lady pronounced that factions would no longer be welcome in Sigil, the Indeps shrugged, took off their faction insignia, and continued business as usual. They'd always said they were never a faction, after all.
== Philosophy ==
This ain't no faction, and ''nobody'' tells us what to do. Keep your options open; nobody's got the key to the truth.
== Role ==
The Indeps run the [[Great Bazaar]], if they could be said to "run" anything. They prefer to be able to live their lives and sell their wares, and not get hassled by the Harmonium.

It was a place of utter cold. {{Quote|Keep your wits about you, and for Gods' sake, keep moving—anything that stops might freeze that way.|A visitor to the Para-Elemental Plane of Ice{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|68-73}}}} ==Description== Much like the [[Elemental Plane of Earth|Plane of Earth]], the Plane of Ice was primarily solid towards its center, though caverns and crevasses cut through the otherwise solid ice in places. Where the plane bordered the Plane of Water, scattered icebergs floated; where it bordered the Plane of Air, the ice ended in a jutting white wall. This solid ice wall was a surface upon which one could walk, a sheet of craggy ice extending in all directions as far as eye could see and where hazardous blizzards scoured. Icy mountain peaks erupted from the surface in places. The air was breathable on this surface, but the temperature was deathly cold. This region of the plane was called the Precipice, and many visitors foolishly thought it to represent the whole plane, though the majority of the plane existed below the Precipice. Gravity existed on this para-plane; up was towards the Plane of Air, while down was towards the Plane of Water. When one approached the "bottom" of the place, more and more water was present until the ice broke up into chunks atop the Plane of Water. This border region was called the Sea of Frozen Lives. Because of how it seemed like the icebergs of the Sea of Frozen Lives seemed to float upon the Plane of Water, some called the Plane of Ice itself the '''Floating Plane''' or the '''Bobbing Plane'''. In the lateral directions, once could travel along the endless ice to the borders of the [[Negative Energy Plane]], the [[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Salt]], the [[Positive Energy Plane]], and the [[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Steam]]. These border regions were known as the Frigid Void, the Stinging Storm, the Shimmering Drifts, and the Fog of Unyielding Frost, respectively. The Frigid Void was free of snow and blizzards and a region of absolute darkness and cold. The Stinging Storm was an area of hailing salt storms. The Fog of Unyielding Frost was full of bitter cold vapors that could freeze one's lungs. The Shimmering Drifts was perhaps the oddest region, as the snow falling here was infused with an energy that could cause severe confusion to those it contacted. [[File:Frostfell_regions-2e.jpg|thumb|300px|''A map of the regions of the Frostfell by their proximity to other Inner Planes.'']] The majority of the plane, however, existed below the Precipice. About half of the caverns within this endless ice were elemental pockets of air; the others were essentially underwater lakes full of ice-cold waters.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|52}} Some boulders were also deeply buried in the ice as well. Not all regions of this para-plane were the same temperature. Some areas could be survived with only mundane means of warmth, but other areas were so cold that only by means of magic could one survive. Some scholars insisted that the plane had some areas so cold that the very words one spoke would freeze solid. In [[Sigil]] some merchants sold bottles of distilled "chaos" and "sadness", prepared from such frozen ideas. Others said that even light itself would freeze here in this "true cold". To reach the Plane of Ice with the ''[[plane shift]]'' spell required a planar fork of [[pewter]], an alloy of [[lead]] and [[tin]]. However, it was risky for travelers from other planes to shift to the Frostfell, for they might end up embedded in the ice. If damage from the cold did not slay them, they would be unable to move. Whether they lived or died, their bodies would be incredibly preserved. If they did not die from the cold, they were likely to be crushed by the extreme pressure of the ice. Travel within the plane was equally dangerous, whether walking atop the Precipice or tunneling deep within the Core Ice, for the entire para-plane was subject to constant shifting and buckling of the ice. There were avalanches and sinkholes and crushing fissures. Besides mundane travel from one of the other Inner Planes, the Para-Plane of Ice could be reached through portals, but few such permanent portals existed naturally. A portal to [[Cania]] was here, and some planewalkers claimed that one existed to [[Muspelheim]] in [[Ysgard]] as well. Two portals to the [[Abyss]] were rumored to exist, one of which was to the [[Layers of the Abyss#Layer 566: Soulfreeze|Soulfreeze]], layer 566. Sometimes, [[elemental vortices]] would connect the Material Plane to the Frostfell, usually from arctic wastelands, terrible blizzards, or the coldest depths of the ocean. ==Government== The Plane of Ice was unique among the [[Para-Elemental Planes]] in that it had a powerful [[archomental]] desiring to establish his realm with the full status of a major [[Elemental Plane]]. Lord [[Cryonax]] longed for ice to be considered the fifth element and wanted the borders of his realm to be the Para-Elemental Planes of Slush and Snow.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|53}} His ambitions even stretched so far that he hoped to supplant the other Elemental Planes altogether! ==Locations== * [[Arcolantha]]{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|73}} * [[Chiseled Estate]], Cryonax's fortress in the very center of the plane. * [[Mountain of Ultimate Winter]]{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|72}} * Ytharior, otherwise known as the "Blood Mire." A frozen lake of blood that formed from an intense battle between [[frost giant|frost giants]], [[ice troll|ice trolls]], and [[snow troll|snow trolls]].{{Cite book/The Inner Planes|72}} ==Inhabitants== Nearly three-quarters of the open caverns with the ice contained life. A little fewer than half of such living creatures found there would be beings of [[air]], while the rest would be beings of ice. In the subterranean lakes, more than a quarter would be beings of [[water]], with the rest being creatures of ice. In both cases, such lifeforms would be immune to the effects of the bitter cold of the water. Most fauna found here were icy, angular counterparts to creatures of the [[Prime Material plane|Prime]], looking much like ice or snow sculptures. Such entities could move freely and unharmed through ice, water, and air in the other Inner Planes. It was also common to find [[yeti]]s, [[remorhaz]]s, and [[white dragon]]s among the plane's inhabitants. Among the more intelligent planar creatures, [[ice mephit|ice mephits]] were native to the plane. [[Marid|Marids]] and [[djinn]] sometimes visited, but neither were native to the Frostfell. The marids often hunted here. [[Frost salamander]]s hunted across the Frostfell, and were in turn hunted by [[azer|azers]] who ventured into the plane to slay the creatures.{{Cite book/Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes|223}} ==Appendix== ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Para-Elemental Planes]] [[Category:Inner Planes]]

During that time, [[baatezu]] were allowed to inform souls of their state and bargain with them.<ref name="TEoC-p221">{{Cite book/The Edge of Chaos|221}}</ref> Souls were offered the chance to become devils themselves, usually starting as a [[lemure]] but having the chance to advance through the devilish ranks, possibly even becoming a [[pit fiend]]. In the wake of that world-shaping event, it merged with the [[House of Nature]] to form the [[Deep Wilds]],<ref name="FRCG4e-63">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|63}}</ref> except for Talos's portion, which the aspect of [[Gruumsh]]<ref name="Dragon378-36">{{Cite dragon/Domains in Eberron and the Forgotten Realms|36}}</ref> took with him to [[Nishrek]].<ref name="FRCG4e-64">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|64}}</ref>
==Description== As a Fiendish plane, Fury's Heart was host to a segment of the [[River of Blood]] which flowed through Malar's realm, the Land of the Hunt. A branch of the river also connected to Umberlee's Blood Sea. Other than [[Astral plane]] travel, the only other known access was via a ''portal'' somewhere beneath the crashing waves of the Blood Sea, connecting it to the [[Fated Depths]].<ref name="PGtF-153" /> The [[Blood Rift]] randomly became coterminous with this plane, allowing creatures and conflict to spill over into Fury's Heart.<ref name="MMIII-35">{{Cite book/Monster Manual III|35}}</ref>
At first glance, this plane was similar to the [[Barrens of Doom and Despair]], with vast stretches of desolation and weather extremes, but unlike the Barrens, this plane was teeming with life that fought tooth and claw for survival. Except for Malar's realm, the whole plane was buffeted by violent storms, thunder and lightning, blizzards of rain, sleet, and snow, and hurricanes. Wind speeds rarely dropped below 31 mph (50 kph) as the Gods of Fury lashed the land and the inhabitants without mercy. In the Land of the Hunt, Malar moderated the weather somewhat to enable tracking skills, scent, spore, vision, and hearing to be more effective, enhancing the thrill of pursuit.<ref name="PGtF-153-154" />
The Land of the Hunt shared a border with the other three realms on this plane. From the shores of the Blood Sea, Malar's vast open plain extended countless miles inland. Where the landscape turned into rocky foothills was the start of Talos's realm, the Towers of Ruin, eventually becoming steep barren hills of stone. In the opposite direction, the temperature eventually began to drop and rolling plain gave way to frozen tundra as the border of Auril's realm, Winter's Hall, was crossed.<ref name="PGtF-153-154" />
==Inhabitants== Petitioners that arrived on this plane often took the form of primitive animals that matched their cruel spirit and evil disposition, [[shark]]s, for example, in Umberlee's realm, and large, land-based carnivores in Malar's realm. For prey to hunt, souls were regularly stolen from the [[Fugue Plane]] and made to take on the form of weaker or timid animals. Other petitioners took on a more elemental form representing the violence and indifference of nature at its worst, such as icy spirits in Winter's Hall or sentient lightning flickering around the Towers of Ruin. Natives of Fury's Heart included [[abrian]]s, [[bloodthorn]], [[ice paraelemental]]s and other cold-natured extremophiles, [[ironmaw]], [[khaasta]], [[myrmixicus]] demons, [[nightmare]]s, fiendish [[squid]], [[phiuhl]], all varieties of [[varrangoin]], [[vorr]], [[vultivor]] [[canomorph]]s, and [[yeth hound]]s.<ref name="PGtF-153-154" /> Near the top of the food chain were various dragons: [[howling dragon]]s, [[pyroclastic dragon]]s, and the [[styx dragon]]s that patrolled the [[River of Blood]].<ref name="DoF-11" /> The pervasive evil of this plane attracted [[night hags]] and [[vargouille]]s to make their home here.<ref name="PGtF-153" /> Due to the occasional connection with the Blood Rift, [[arrow demon]]s could be found on this plane.<ref name="MMIII-35" />
==Realms== * [[Auril]]'s realm of Winter's Hall was the coldest place in all the [[plane]]s. Her throne was made of blue flames, frozen in place and shaped to her liking. Her palace was constructed of bitterly cold ''[[wind wall]]s''.<ref name="PGtF-153" /> * [[Malar]]'s Land of the Hunt was a vast open plain kept well stocked with game for sport. Intruders were very likely to become the next quarry.<ref name="PGtF-153-154" /> * [[Talos]] kept the winds constantly blowing outward from his Towers of Ruin; the raging hurricane at the center gradually died down to mere strong gusts at the borders. The Storm Lord's "palace" was mainly rubble haphazardly stacked into "towers" etched by the wind and subject to random and frequent lightning strikes. At his whim, pelting rain and targeted lightning bolts joined the storm to drive off unwelcome guests.<ref name="PGtF-154">{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|154}}</ref> * [[Umberlee]] swam in her reddish salt-water sea beneath foamy waves churned by constant storms of pounding rain, gale-force winds, and lightning—near-certain destruction for anything that attempted to breach the surface or brave the waves.<ref name="PGtF-154" />
